findings.title: Applied-vs-reported noise magnitude is untested on four sibling noise paths: 5% shortfalls survive the whole suite (OPQ-378 fix, #833, covers only the scalar DP-SGD path)
findings.claim:
OPQ-378 (#833, closed) was fixed by adding one high-n conformance test per mechanism that ties the realized second moment of the drawn noise to the reported NoisedPytree.noise_stddev: packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py:133-142 (scalar gaussian_noise, n=1e6, tol 6/sqrt(2n)=4.2e-3, with a *0.97 negative control) and packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_realized_stddev.py:41-48 + 100-155 (all six MF strategies, same shape). Four sibling paths that draw noise through *different* code were not covered, and mutation shows each accepts a 5% divergence between the noise actually drawn and the sigma the accountant is charged for. Verified by injecting the defect and running the owning suites at HEAD 12146ec4 (native ext rebuilt from source; clean baseline 4590 passed / 2 network-flaky failures):
 (a) per-group DP-SGD Gaussian - `_sample(tensor, 0.95 * group_std, generator)` at _gaussian.py:226 -> 1355 passed, 26 skipped (opaque-dpsgd + opaque-engine); re-run WIDE over opaque-dpsgd, opaque-engine, opaque-dpftrl, opaque-optimizers, opaque-accounting, opaque-base, opaque-auditing, opaque-transformers and the root tests/ integration tree it is still 3677 passed, 42 skipped, 0 failed. The only magnitude assertion on this path is a RATIO, packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_per_group_noise.py:48-50 `assert mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5` on 100 samples, which a uniform scale factor leaves invariant by construction.
 (b) paired second-moment stream - `second_stddev * 0.95` at _gaussian.py:274-276 -> 1346 passed, 2 skipped (opaque-dpsgd + opaque-dpftrl). packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_gaussian_second_moment.py uses torch.zeros(10) and asserts only the reported metadata (lines 52-71, 77-107).
 (c) per-group MF (DP-FTRL) - `noise * leaf_std * 0.95` at _engine.py:156 -> 620 passed (opaque-dpftrl). packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_per_group_noise.py contains no realized-sample statistic at all (no .std(), .var() or square().mean() anywhere in the file); its Mahalanobis checks (lines 426-455) read NoisedPytree.noise_stddev.
 (d) AdaClip quantile noise - `* fraction_noise_std * 0.95` at _adaptive.py:121 -> 1523 passed, 26 skipped (opaque-dpsgd + opaque-engine + tests/integration). packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/clipping/test_adaptive_quantile_noise.py has nine tests, none measuring the realized noise scale.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor of any of these four draw sites (an fp32<->bf16 round trip, a PerGroup lookup that resolves a stale bound, a Mahalanobis re-derivation, a change to the quantile-noise default) that loses ~5% of the intended noise ships green. Measured cost at HEAD with opaque's own accountant: (a) per-group and (c) per-group MF at nm=1.0 behave like nm=0.95, so a run reported as eps=1.828322 (q=0.01, 1000 steps, delta=1e-5) actually delivers eps=2.042989 (+11.7%). (b) scaling only the squared stream by 0.95 breaks the joint Mahalanobis budget sum_i (Delta_i/sigma_i)^2 <= 1/nm^2 (it becomes 1.054/nm^2), i.e. an effective nm of 0.974039, so reported 1.828322 is really 1.933575 (+5.8%). (d) with adaclip(gaussian(1.0), expected_batch_size=16, num_groups=8) a 5% quantile-noise shortfall takes the true epsilon from 14.047962 to 15.972834 (+13.7%); at 0.5x it is 94.276769. All four are silent.

findings.fix_sketch: Extend the OPQ-378 pattern to the sibling draw sites rather than the mechanism entry points. Parametrize `_assert_realized_stddev_matches_reported` over (i) gaussian_noise with a PerGroup max_norm, asserting per-leaf RMS against `output.noise_stddev.for_path(path)` for each group; (ii) the paired SecondMomentClippingOutput input, asserting both streams separately; (iii) mf_gaussian_noise with a PerGroup max_norm for at least identity and one correlated strategy; and (iv) adaptive_clipped_grad, collecting the per-step noisy clipping rate over >=1e5 steps and asserting its sample stddev against fraction_noise_std at 5/sqrt(2n). Keep the existing negative control (`* 0.97` must raise) on each new case so the tolerance cannot silently widen. Sizing the per-group tensors at 1e6 elements keeps the gate at ~0.4%.

findings.title: A GPU runner with <24 GB silently skips the entire Triton kernel suite (397 tests, 225 CUDA-selected) and the CUDA lane still reports green
findings.claim: `pytest_collection_modifyitems` in the kernels conftest reads `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory` and, when it is below MIN_KERNEL_CUDA_MEM_GB = 24, attaches `pytest.mark.skip` to EVERY collected item whose path is under the kernels directory - not just the stress/perf tests its reason string names. That directory holds the numerical correctness suite for every fused kernel (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, GeGLU, RoPE, cross-entropy, linear-CE, LoRA, MoE, autocast, vmap-grad parity). pytest then exits 0 with everything skipped, `run_python_test_package.sh` records the path as a success (the exit-5 branch is not reached), and the lane is green. The CUDA preflight added by 039fc012 (#876) to close OPQ-377 asserts only that a CUDA device exists and can do arithmetic - it does not check memory - so it cannot distinguish this case from a real run.
findings.failure_scenario: The self-hosted GPU runner is re-provisioned onto a smaller card (a 16 GB A4000/T4/L4 is the common case) or the label GPU-runner-001 is repointed. All three CUDA lanes on pr.yml and all three on ci.yml then run `-m 'cuda and not slow'` / `-m cuda`, collect 225 kernel tests, skip 100% of them at collection, and pass. publish-dev-wheels (ci.yml:199-213) needs exactly those jobs, so main keeps publishing wheels whose Triton kernels - the code path the DP-SGD vmap(grad) pipeline runs on GPU - has had zero validation. The lane passes `-rs`, so the skips appear in the log, but nothing fails on them.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/conftest.py:20 `MIN_KERNEL_CUDA_MEM_GB = 24`

packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/conftest.py:36-48 - builds `skip_marker` then `for item in items: if Path(str(item.fspath)).resolve().is_relative_to(kernels_dir): item.add_marker(skip_marker)`; there is no stress/perf predicate

functional proof: loading that conftest, stubbing torch.cuda.is_available()->True and get_device_properties()->16 GiB, and passing it fake items for all 19 test files under kernels/ plus one dpsgd item marks 19/19 kernel files and 0 non-kernel items, reason 'Kernel stress tests require >= 24GB CUDA memory (found 16.00GB).'
collection at HEAD: `pytest --collect-only -m 'cuda and not slow' packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels` -> 225/397 tests collected
.github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:38-48 - only exit code 5 is special-cased; an all-skipped run exits 0 and is recorded as a success
.github/scripts/assert_cuda_available.sh:24-52 - the preflight probes is_available(), device_count() and one tensor add; no memory check
.github/workflows/ci.yml:199-213 - publish-dev-wheels needs python-tests-cuda / -cuda-minimum / -cuda-latest
findings.fix_sketch: Scope the gate to the tests it was written for: mark the stress/perf cases explicitly (e.g. `@pytest.mark.kernel_stress`) and skip only those, leaving the numerical-parity tests to run at whatever size the card allows (most already use tiny shapes; only the MELLUM_CONFIG perf cases need 24 GB). Independently, make the lane fail rather than pass on a fully-skipped selection: have run_python_test_package.sh parse the summary (or use a `--strict-nonempty` plugin) and fail when selected > 0 and passed == 0, and extend assert_cuda_available.sh with a minimum-memory assertion keyed to MIN_KERNEL_CUDA_MEM_GB so a too-small card fails the lane instead of emptying it.

findings.title: Open issue #880 is materially wider than its title: 87 CUDA-requiring tests across 13 files in 5 packages carry a skipif but no `cuda` marker, so they run in no CI lane
findings.line: 35-37 (module pytestmark); see evidence for the full 13-file list
findings.claim: AGENTS.md makes the `cuda` marker the selection contract: non-CUDA lanes run `-m 'not cuda ...'` and the CUDA lanes run `-m 'cuda and not slow'` / `-m cuda`. A test that requires CUDA through a bare `skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available())` and omits the marker is therefore SELECTED-then-skipped on every CPU lane and DESELECTED on every CUDA lane - it executes nowhere. Open issue #880 scopes this to 'LoRA and linear-CE kernel tests'. An AST walk over every test file at HEAD (module pytestmark, class decorators and function decorators) finds 87 such test functions in 13 files across five packages; test_lora.py (27) and test_linear_cross_entropy.py (22) are the 49 #880 names, leaving 38 outside its scope, including whole files. The delta made it worse rather than better: 720 net lines were added to five of these unrunnable files during these 124 commits (test_lora.py +495, test_linear_cross_entropy.py +243, test_autocast.py, test_compile.py, test_kernel_patches.py) without any of the commits adding the marker.
findings.failure_scenario: opaque-alignment's entire GPU test surface is unreachable: its four `TestVmapAutocastBf16` cases - the only tests that pin `vmap(grad(fused_nll/dft/sequence_logp))` under `autocast(bf16, cuda)`, i.e. the per-sample gradient path DP-SGD actually runs on a GPU - collect 5 under the PR CPU marker (all skipped at runtime) and 0 under `cuda and not slow`. Same for opaque-patches/test_autocast.py (26 collected on CPU, 0 on the CUDA lane), opaque-engine/test_memory.py and opaque-dpsgd/test_compile.py (0 collected on the CUDA lane). Because `packages/opaque-alignment` and the foundation packages collect zero CUDA-marked tests at all, their legs on every CUDA lane also hit the exit-5 escape hatch and pass empty. A fused-kernel change that breaks bf16 autocast gradients ships with a green CUDA gate.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_vmap_autocast_bf16.py:121 `@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason='CUDA required')` on class TestVmapAutocastBf16, no mark.cuda anywhere in the file
packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/test_autocast.py:35-37 module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), ...)`, no mark.cuda

measured: `--collect-only -m 'cuda and not slow'` gives 'no tests collected (26 deselected)' for test_autocast.py, '(5 deselected)' for test_vmap_autocast_bf16.py, '(16 deselected)' for opaque-engine/tests/profiling/test_memory.py, '(13 deselected)' for opaque-dpsgd/tests/functional/test_compile.py; the same files collect 26 and 5 under the PR CPU marker
measured: `--collect-only -m cuda` collects 0 for packages/opaque-base, packages/opaque-accounting, packages/opaque-auditing and packages/opaque-alignment

unmarked counts per file (87 total): opaque-alignment logprob/test_logprob.py:299 (1), sft/loss/test_dft.py:346 (1), sft/loss/test_nll.py:292 (1), test_vmap_autocast_bf16.py:121 class (4); opaque-dpsgd functional/test_compile.py:191,223 (2); opaque-engine profiling/test_memory.py:73 (1); opaque-patches kernels/test_autocast.py (12), kernels/test_compile.py (3), kernels/test_linear_cross_entropy.py (22), kernels/test_lora.py (27), transformers/components/test_batchify.py:7-10 (3); opaque-transformers test_kernel_patches.py:18-21 (9), test_precision_training.py:129 (1)

AGENTS.md 'Test markers' and 'CI lane marker expressions' sections define the contract
findings.fix_sketch: Treat the marker as the single source of truth and derive the skip from it: delete the ad-hoc `skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available())` module/class guards and replace them with `pytest.mark.cuda`, which the repo-root conftest already turns into a runtime skip (conftest.py:36-42). Then add a guard test (or a ruff/AST check in the autoformat lane) that fails when a file mentions `cuda.is_available` in a skipif without a sibling `mark.cuda`, so the class cannot regrow. Widen #880's scope to the 13 files.

findings.title: OPQ-381 was closed (#836) without a change: exit-5 is still converted to success and two of five distributed-lane legs plus the foundation leg of every CUDA lane still pass on zero tests
findings.claim: OPQ-381 asked for a per-suite minimum-test floor. The runner is unchanged: `if [[ "$status" -eq 5 && "$ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION" == "true" ]]; then ... exit 0`, and `allow-empty-test-selection: true` is still set on the distributed lane and all three CUDA lanes in both pr.yml (lines 81, 145, 160, 177) and ci.yml (41, 100, 112, 126). `git log 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh` shows the only delta commit touching it is 039fc012 (#876), which added the CUDA preflight (OPQ-377) and left the exit-5 branch alone. Measured per-path collection at HEAD under the distributed lane's exact marker (`distributed and not cuda`): opaque-base 0, opaque-accounting 0, opaque-auditing 0, opaque-patches 0, tests 0 - so the 'Foundation' and 'Integration' legs still pass having executed nothing, exactly as OPQ-381 measured in August. Under `-m cuda` the foundation trio and opaque-alignment also collect 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor that drops, renames or mis-applies the `distributed` marker (or the `cuda` marker - see the 87-test marker gap) makes every leg of that lane collect nothing; all legs convert exit 5 to success and the lane reports green. ci.yml:199-213 makes publish-dev-wheels depend on exactly those job results, so main keeps publishing wheels with the collective-desync and GPU regression classes unguarded. The lane's green check carries no information about whether it ran 12 tests or 0, and nothing downstream reads TEST_RESULTS_FILE.

Pair it with the all-skipped check from the kernel-conftest finding so 'collected N, ran 0' also fails. Then drop allow-empty-test-selection from the lanes whose suites do select tests.

findings.title: OPQ-386 was closed (#841) without a change: Python 3.12 still executes zero tests while all ten wheels advertise it
findings.claim: OPQ-386 asked for either one cheap 3.12 leg or dropping the classifier claim. Neither happened. `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` over the current tree returns nothing at all; validate-distributions.yml still matrixes `python-version: ['3.11', '3.13']`, python-tests.yml's input still defaults to 3.11, and the dependency-boundary lanes are pinned to 3.11 and 3.13. Meanwhile every one of the ten package pyprojects still carries `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` and `requires-python = '>=3.11,<3.14'`, and there is no documented endpoints-only policy anywhere in CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md or docs/ (the only 3.12 mention outside pyproject classifiers is AGENTS.md:326, which notes 3.12 is the Cursor VM's default interpreter).
findings.failure_scenario: A 3.12-only regression - an interpreter-specific behaviour in the torch.func vmap/pytree layer, or a dependency resolving to a different wheel on 3.12 - ships in a release whose metadata explicitly advertises 3.12, with no CI signal that ever existed. Bounded: 3.11 and 3.13 bracket most such behaviour, and nothing here changes a privacy guarantee. The specific irony is that AGENTS.md tells agents the development VM runs 3.12, so the interpreter contributors use locally is the one CI never exercises.
evidence: `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` -> no matches
.github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml:19 `python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]`
.github/workflows/python-tests.yml:34-38 - python-version input defaults to "3.11"
packages/*/pyproject.toml:21 (23/26/28 for accounting/alignment/transformers) - `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` in all ten, plus pyproject.toml:29
packages/*/pyproject.toml:10-12 - `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"`
AGENTS.md:326 - '**Python 3.12** (system default on the VM) satisfies the `>=3.11,<3.14` constraint'
findings.fix_sketch: Cheapest close: add "3.12" to the validate-distributions matrix (it only installs the built wheels and runs one cross-stack scenario, so the marginal cost is one ubuntu-latest job). Otherwise drop the 3.12 classifier from all ten pyprojects and state the endpoints-only policy in CONTRIBUTING.md so the metadata stops promising coverage that does not exist.

findings.title: A shipped feature's only integration regression tests are gated behind a capability probe that turns the feature's removal into a silent skip
findings.claim: `TestPerGroupAutoSxMf` (2 test methods x 6 strategies = 12 tests, the only integration coverage of AUTO-S clipping composed with per-group MF noise) is guarded by an autouse fixture that calls `_per_group_supported_by_mf_noise()`, which invokes `mf_gaussian_noise` with a PerGroup bound and returns False if it raises a TypeError mentioning 'PerGroup'. On False the fixture calls `pytest.skip('... test pending PR #192 (per-group MF noise).')`. PR #192 has long since landed - I verified the probe returns True at HEAD, so the tests do run today - but the gate remains, and opaque's public exception taxonomy makes the failure mode live: `opaque.exceptions.InputTypeError` derives from TypeError (packages/opaque-base/tests/test_exceptions.py:23 pins `issubclass(InputTypeError, (OpaqueError, TypeError))`), and `_expect_clipped` / `_iid_normal_noise` raise exactly that with 'PerGroup' in the message.
findings.failure_scenario: Any future change that re-rejects PerGroup bounds in mf_gaussian_noise - a tightened `_expect_clipped`, a PerGroup path lost in a refactor of `_iid_normal_noise` - converts 12 integration tests from FAIL to SKIP. The lane stays green and the loss of per-group MF support is invisible. Same shape as the OPQ-382 pattern the team just fixed in test_trl_trainers.py by replacing a self-skip with a fail-closed fixture.
evidence: tests/integration/noise/test_auto_clipping_mf_noise.py:132-154 `_per_group_supported_by_mf_noise()` with `except TypeError as exc: if 'PerGroup' in str(exc): return False`
tests/integration/noise/test_auto_clipping_mf_noise.py:333-340 autouse `_gate` fixture calling pytest.skip
the docstrings at :36 and :330-333 still say 'On plain main mf_gaussian_noise rejects PerGroup bounds ... PR #192 removes that gate'
verified at HEAD by running the probe body standalone: 'PROBE -> supported=True', so the 12 tests currently execute
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_engine.py:133-156 - the PerGroup branch exists and raises InputTypeError mentioning 'PerGroup' for non-tensor leaves
findings.fix_sketch: Delete `_per_group_supported_by_mf_noise` and the `_gate` fixture. Per-group MF noise is shipped and documented (docs/user-guide/noise.md:95-127), so its regression tests should fail, not skip, when it stops working. If a capability probe is genuinely wanted, invert it into an assertion in a single test (`test_mf_gaussian_noise_accepts_per_group_bounds`) and let the other twelve run unconditionally.

findings.title: Two load-best-model checkpoint-correctness tests skip themselves exactly when the behaviour they guard is broken
findings.claim: `TestLoadBestModelMutates::test_save_model_after_load_best_sees_best_weights` runs a trainer with `load_best_model_at_end=True` and then does `if trainer.state.best_model_checkpoint is None: pytest.skip('Eval never improved; nothing to compare.')`, plus a second skip if the adapter file is missing. `TestBestFolderLookup::test_best_folder_lookup` does the same on `trainer.state.best_global_step is None`. Both preconditions are precisely the observable symptom of the defect the tests exist to catch: a regression that stops the trainer recording a best checkpoint makes both tests skip rather than fail. I verified they currently pass (3 passed in 11.82s), so this is latent, not active.
findings.failure_scenario: A change to the DP trainer's metric bookkeeping (the delta reworked `_dp_trainer.py` heavily: +227 lines in 87404a1b alone) that leaves `state.best_model_checkpoint`/`best_global_step` unset silently disables the only two tests asserting that `save_model()` after `load_best_model_at_end` writes the best weights and that the best-checkpoint folder lookup resolves correctly. Users then export the last-step weights while believing they exported the best ones, with no CI signal.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_checkpoint_correctness.py:166-167 `if trainer.state.best_model_checkpoint is None: pytest.skip("Eval never improved; nothing to compare.")`
packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_checkpoint_correctness.py:173-174 second skip on a missing adapter_model.safetensors
packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_checkpoint_correctness.py:283-284 `if trainer.state.best_global_step is None: pytest.skip("Eval never improved; nothing to verify.")`
ran both classes at HEAD: '3 passed in 11.82s' - the guards are inert today
findings.fix_sketch: Make the precondition an assertion. The fixtures use a deterministic tiny dataset with eval_strategy='steps', eval_steps=2, metric_for_best_model='eval_loss', so a best checkpoint is expected every run: replace the two skips with `assert trainer.state.best_model_checkpoint is not None` / `assert trainer.state.best_global_step is not None` (and keep the adapter-file check as an assert too). If a run can legitimately produce no improvement, force one by seeding the eval metric rather than by skipping.

clean_areas: Mutation method and baseline: every result below comes from editing the shipped source at HEAD 12146ec4, clearing __pycache__, running the owning package suites under the PR-gate marker (`-m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed'`, -n 8), then restoring the file (harness at scratchpad/mut2/run.py; raw results in results-b1.json / b2.log / b3.log; `git status` clean afterwards). The pre-built native accounting extension in the working tree was stale (Aug 27, missing `poisson_pld` added by #850) and produced 88 spurious failures; I rebuilt it with `cargo build --release --features python-extension` before baselining. Clean baseline (full PR-gate selection, -n 12, 22m42s): 4590 passed / 191 skipped / 2 failed. Both failures - test_dp_guarantees.py::test_resume_from_save_only_model_checkpoint_is_refused and test_dp_trainer.py::TestDPTrainerTrainerContractFlags::test_explicit_train_ignores_do_train_flag - pass in isolation (7.01s and 6.22s) and inside the -n 8 mutation runs, and the same run logged repeated `[Errno 104] Connection reset by peer` on Hugging Face `gpt2` lookups, so I treated them as sandbox network/parallelism flakes rather than defects; they are the only non-determinism I saw in 12 full-suite executions.

Clipping bound enforcement is the best-tested invariant in the repository. Mutation M3 (`ratio = clipping_norm_tensor / norm * 1.05` in clip_pytree, _pytree.py:626) -> 42 failed; mutation M4, removing the conservative ULP margin (`relative = 1.0 - rounding - 2.0 * norm_roundoff` -> `relative = 1.0` in _guard_scale, _pytree.py:139) -> 38 failed. Both are caught by packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping/test_clipping_numerics.py across 4 dtypes x 5 shapes (test_clip_pytree_bound_holds_in_stored_dtype), leaf counts 1..600, a float64-accumulator-free path, per-group bounds, complex leaves, and an explicit test_guard_is_negligible_at_float32.

Per-sample gradient isolation through the microbatch path. Mutation M5 (slice reuse: `x[s:e]` -> `x[0:e-s]` in _microbatch_accumulate_reduced, _clipped_fun.py:258-262, so every microbatch re-clips the first k examples and the summed sensitivity becomes k*C) -> 24 failed across opaque-engine and opaque-dpsgd, including the microbatch/full-batch equivalence tests for clipped_grad, clipped_fun, auto_clipped_grad, adaptive_clipped_grad, second moments, and low-precision accumulation.

Reported per-example sensitivity (the ClippedPytree.max_norm the noise mechanism is calibrated from). Scalar DP-SGD Gaussian applied-vs-reported noise (the OPQ-378 fix, #833). Poisson sampler conformance to its amplification model. Mutation M6 (replace the Bernoulli draw in _plain_poisson_step_indices with `rng.choice(num_examples, size=round(n*q), replace=False)` - a fixed-size sample with the same expected batch size, which breaks Poisson amplification while preserving the mean) -> 5 failed, including test_poisson.py::test_statistical_properties_variance, ::test_iteration_produces_variable_batches, test_sampler_keys.py::test_poisson_matches_numpy_generator and the cross-rank independence test. The suite therefore pins the batch-size distribution, not just its mean.

Composition count. Mutation M7 (`Repeated.pld` forwarding `max(1, self.count - 1)` to `inner.repeated_pld`, _repeated.py:71-72 (`self.inner.repeated_pld(self.count, ...)`)) -> 39 failed, essentially all in packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_cross_validation.py against Google dp_accounting and riskcal (epsilon, delta, advantage, beta, 3000-step cases) plus test_identity_mf.py::test_self_compose_matches_repeated_gaussian. Worth noting what does NOT catch it: the trainer-level guard test_dp_guarantees.py::test_accountant_composes_exactly_total_steps builds its 'independent' reference with `for _ in range(n): acc |= step`, and I verified that the Accountant merges that into exactly the same object the trainer uses (`repr(acc.process)` == `repr(step*5)` == `Repeated(inner=Poisson(...), count=5)`), so it pins the step COUNT but not the composition arithmetic. The independent oracle is the cross-validation suite, and it is present and effective.

Sampler RNG continuity across resume. Mutation M8 (dropping the `for _ in range(consumed): sampler._sample_step()` replay in _from_state_dict_poisson, _poisson.py:264-265) -> 4 failed, including test_poisson_state_dict.py::test_snapshot_at_step_k_resumes_with_matching_remainder (which loads into a template built from a DIFFERENT seed, so it cannot be satisfied by the template's own stream) and the trainer-level test_dp_trainer.py::test_resume_normalizes_prefetched_legacy_sampler_cursor.

Noise stream advancement within a run.
